A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GLES case study. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–G are readable and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: Sections 4.1–4.3 report original model comparisons, longitudinal analyses, and demographic-prompt ablations. Appendices E and G provide additional qualitative and quantitative results.

after.justification: v2 retains the original model-comparison, wave-analysis, and ablation results, including the numerical tables and qualitative examples in the appendices.

M1.justification: The six-variable persona prompts, three generation models, and fine-tuned German BERT response classifier remain unchanged. Figures 2 and 9 and Table 8 retain the same generation and ablation prompts.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same GLES open-ended question, German demographic groups, and survey waves. The additional German and US election-knowledge probes in Table 15 are also retained.

E2.justification: Gemma, Llama2, and Mixtral remain the evaluated models, with the same prompt-ablation comparisons and survey-resampling comparator in Table 11. The newly cited fine-tuning approaches are future alternatives, not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The wave-12 comparison, waves-12–21 analysis, missing-feature exclusion, 1,500 annotated responses, 16-class coding, evaluation metrics, and ablation design are unchanged. The rephrased source-survey question does not establish a changed experimental procedure.

E4.justification: The demographic-variable ablations, subgroup and temporal analyses, qualitative failure analysis, and factual-knowledge examples are retained. Appendix reflow does not add or remove an analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions already report mean and standard deviation across waves in Figure 13 and the same base-prompt variation in Section 4.3. No seed information, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: The numerical tables and qualitative examples are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains JS distances of 0.62, 0.28, and 0.29 for Gemma, Llama2, and Mixtral. Figure 1 simplifies the display to five categories; category-level wave results remain in Table 13.

T1.justification: Equations 1–9, the metric definitions, and the conditional-probability argument about silicon sampling in Section 5 are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are introduced or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract and main contributions retain the same claims about Llama2's relative alignment, uneven subgroup representation, political bias, and demographic-prompt effects. The shortened conclusion preserves their scope.

C2.justification: The Limitations section newly identifies reliance on zero-shot prompting as an applicability boundary and proposes evaluating fine-tuning in the German context. Existing interpretations of diversity, political bias, and prompt sensitivity remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The code-access statement, annotation instructions, prompt templates, software versions, quantization, batch sizes, classifier hyperparameters, and reported computation times are retained in the main text and Appendices A–D.

R1.justification: v2 adds Cao et al. (2025) and Holtdirk et al. (2025) when discussing fine-tuning as future work. Publication updates for existing references, including von der Heyde et al., do not represent additional research comparisons or a substantial repositioning.

P1.justification: Localized edits rephrase the survey question, replace ablation shorthand with descriptive wording, clarify a discussion heading, and condense the conclusion. The section structure and most prose remain intact; an author affiliation is also updated.

P2.justification: Figure 1 shows only the five leading categories, Figure 4 changes proportions and moves its legend, and Figure 9 uses larger prompt text. Figure 7's caption explains the ablation labels. These are limited display changes alongside appendix reflow.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves readability through simpler displays, more legible German prompt text, and clearer ablation descriptions. The explicit zero-shot limitation and references to fine-tuning better delimit the findings. The experimental evidence and principal conclusions remain unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
